outline.chapter_title: Introduction to Mathematical Reasoning with Large Language Models
outline.description: Sets the stage by explaining why mathematical reasoning is challenging for LLMs, reviews the landscape of existing models, and motivates the need for open‑source solutions like DeepSeekMath.
subtopics: The nature of mathematical reasoning for AI
Benchmark landscape: MATH, GSM8K, geometry tasks
Limitations of closed‑source models vs. open‑source baselines
Overview of DeepSeekMath objectives and contributions

outline.chapter_title: Building a Large‑Scale Math Corpus from the Web
outline.description: Describes the data‑collection pipeline that turns raw Common Crawl data into a high‑quality, multilingual math pre‑training corpus.
subtopics: Seed corpus selection (OpenWebMath) and fastText classifier basics
Iterative retrieval, ranking, and domain‑level expansion
Deduplication, token budgeting, and stopping criteria
Decontamination: preventing benchmark leakage
Comparative analysis with MathPile, Proof‑Pile‑2, and OpenWebMath

outline.description: Explains model initialization, training schedule, and the impact of the math corpus on model performance.
subtopics: Why start from a code‑oriented checkpoint (DeepSeek‑Coder‑Base)
Token mix: math, code, natural language, multilingual balance
Training hyperparameters and infrastructure (HAI‑LLM)
Evaluation methodology: few‑shot chain‑of‑thought prompting
Results on quantitative reasoning, tool‑augmented solving, formal proof, and general NLP benchmarks

outline.description: Covers the construction of the instruction‑tuning dataset and the fine‑tuning process that yields DeepSeekMath‑Instruct 7B.
subtopics: Data sources: GSM8K, MATH, MathInstruct, Chinese K‑12 corpora
Formats: Chain‑of‑Thought, Program‑of‑Thought, Tool‑Integrated Reasoning
"Data curation pipeline and quality control"
"Training regime: batch size, learning rate schedule, context handling"
"Evaluation against closed and open models on MATH and other benchmarks"

outline.description: Introduces RL fine‑tuning, focusing on the novel Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) algorithm and its practical advantages.
subtopics: "Recap of PPO for LLMs"
"Motivation for removing the critic model"
"Derivation of GRPO objective and baseline estimation"
"Outcome vs. process supervision"
"Iterative GRPO with reward model updates"
"Training details: sampling groups, KL regularization, hyperparameters"
